actions.name: create_comment
actions.description: Create a Notion comment: on a page or block through parent, or as a reply in an existing discussion through discussion_id. The integration needs the insert comments capability; without the read comments capability Notion returns only the new comment's object and id.

block_id.description: The block to attach the comment to.

parent.description: The page or block that starts a new discussion.

discussion_id.description: The discussion thread to reply in.

rich_text.description: The comment body as Notion rich text objects.

file_upload_id.description: The ID of a Notion file upload whose status is uploaded.

attachments.description: Up to 3 uploaded files to attach to the comment.

type.description: Show the name given in custom.

display_name.description: The author name Notion shows on the comment.

inputSchema.description: The input payload for this action.

discussion_id.description: The discussion thread the comment belongs to.

created_time.description: The time when the comment was created.

last_edited_time.description: The time when the comment was last edited.

type.description: How the author name was chosen.

anyOf.description: The author name Notion shows on the comment.

resolved_name.description: The author name Notion shows on the comment.

display_name.description: The author name shown on the comment.

actions.name: get_current_user
actions.description: The workspace and owning user of the connected Notion credential, read from what was stored with it: the OAuth grant, or the bot object recorded when the credential was validated. Makes no API call. An internal integration answers with its workspace and no user.

workspaceId.description: The Notion workspace the grant was issued in.

anyOf.description: The workspace's display name, when the grant carried one.

workspaceName.description: The workspace's display name, when the grant carried one.

anyOf.description: The person who authorized the grant. Null when the grant names no user.

userId.description: The person who authorized the grant. Null when the grant names no user.

anyOf.description: That person's display name, when the grant carried one.

userName.description: That person's display name, when the grant carried one.

isBot.description: Whether the credential resolves to a bot rather than a person.

outputSchema.description: The workspace and owning user of the connected Notion credential.

actions.name: retrieve_page_markdown
actions.description: Retrieve a Notion page or block subtree rendered as enhanced Markdown.

includeTranscript.description: Whether to include meeting note transcripts.

inputSchema.description: The input payload for this action.

object.description: Notion's object tag for the rendered result.

id.description: The id Notion echoes for the rendered page, in Notion's own spelling.

markdown.description: The page rendered as enhanced Markdown. An empty string for a page with no content.

truncated.description: Whether the render stopped short of the whole page (Notion renders roughly 20,000 blocks at most). Resubmit the ids in unknown_block_ids to fetch what was left out.

unknown_block_ids.description: Blocks rendered as <unknown>: truncated subtrees, children this grant cannot read, and unsupported block types. Non-empty on many complete pages, so not on its own a sign of a partial render.

pageId.description: The page or block id the render was requested for, exactly as given in the input. Notion may spell an id dashed or undashed in its own body, so a consumer joining rows to bindings needs the spelling it asked with.

lastEditedTime.description: When the page or block was last edited, read from its own object — the markdown response carries no revision.

outputSchema.description: A Notion page rendered as Markdown, with its revision and how complete the render was.
